subject: Recap + Ops Checklist: Reserved GPU Discovery for Helix Labs
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Torres <emma@helixlabs.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + Ops Checklist: Reserved GPU Discovery for Helix Labs

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick written recap to make sure we’re aligned and to capture the immediate ops/next-step checklist. Please flag anything I misremembered.

Summary of pain & goals (from Helix):
- Peak-sensitive inference for multimodal clinical assistant: 500–1,200 qps burst, steady-state ~150 qps.
- Strict isolation requirement for patient-derived data (want a dedicated, VPC-isolated pool).
- Model: custom fine-tuned 70B decoder (currently FP16, evaluating 4-bit quantization).
- Latency SLO: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 100ms, p99 target ~120ms for text-only calls.
- Throughput expectation: sustained token throughput of ~300k tokens/min with spike handling to 1M tokens/min.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and audit logs required.

Operational constraints you called out:
- Prefer reserved capacity with burst-to-shared as fallback for traffic spikes.
- Need canary rollout plan for model updates; want automatic rollback on latency/quality regressions.
- Ramp timeline: target pilot in Q4, production by end of Q1 2027, procurement sign-off required.

Our proposed dedicated-capacity approach (high level):
- Reserved GPU pool (isolation): 6 x A100-equivalent nodes initially (configurable), with autoscale window and burst to hosted nodes up to additional 8 nodes.
- KV cache + prefix caching for common prompts to reduce cold-start tokens.
- Quantization support path: we’ll validate 4-bit perf/quality profile on your finetuned model.
- Canary rollout + continuous eval hooks: integrate your prompt sets for automatic quality/regression alerts.
- Observability: token-level cost, p95/p99 traces, and audit logs for all inference requests.

Immediate action items (owners & ETA):
- Helix: share sample workload traces (1 week) — Emma / procurement (Procurement to authorize trace share).
- Redwood (Markus): deliver an ops-playbook draft + sizing worksheet (attached) with two configuration options (conservative and optimized) — ETA 48 hours.
- Redwood (Neha): validate SOC 2 artifacts and provide list of evidence required for Helix’s audit team — ETA 3 business days.
- Helix: confirm procurement timeline & PO format so we can align pricing cadence — Emma / Procurement — ETA EOD next Tue.

Attachments I’m sharing: redwood_capacity_playbook_v1.pdf (ops playbook & sizing), draft_sla_helix.docx (SLA example for reserved pools).

If that all looks right, I’ll schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week to walk through the sizing worksheet and procurement steps.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference runtime
From: Emma Torres <emma@helixlabs.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@helixlabs.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 18:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + Ops Checklist: Reserved GPU Discovery for Helix Labs

Markus — thanks, this is great and matches our notes. A few clarifications:
- The 70B model is currently served at FP16; we want the quantization path but need to validate quality on ~12k prompt examples (we’ll share).
- For compliance, we’ll need a formal list of log retention windows and encryption-at-rest details (Neha — if you can include that in your artifact list that would be ideal).
- Procurement: our PO approval will likely be a 3–4 week process after legal reviews; we may need a one-time pilot pricing arrangement to get the pilot signed sooner.

Next steps from Helix: I’ll coordinate the trace export and the prompt set with our infra team and send by 9/10. Procurement is looped here (procure@helixlabs.ai) to confirm the PO timeline.

Appreciate the quick turn on the playbook — look forward to the sizing options.

—Emma
Emma Torres
Head of ML Infrastructure, Helix Labs
emma@helixlabs.ai

Emma — thanks for the quick confirmation. We’ll proceed as follows:
1) I attached the ops playbook + SLA draft in my original note; Ben will follow up with pilot + committed pricing by EOD tomorrow.
2) Neha will send the SOC2/evidence checklist and retention details by end of week.
3) Proposed calendar: 30-min walkthrough on Sep 9 at 10:00 PT — calendar: https://cal.example.com/markus/helix-reserved-pool-1. If that time doesn’t work, propose two alternatives.

Operational notes for the walkthrough:
- We’ll run a short live perf demo (30 minutes) in a sandbox k8s cluster using a quantized variant; please ensure your infra can share the trace by then.
- We’ll show the canary rollout and automated rollback on a synthetic regression trigger so your SRE team can validate the runbook.

If procurement needs a short summary doc for legal, we can produce a one-page procurement brief with PO language and a burst clause (Ben).

Looking forward —
Markus
